body.statement: Can the construction in def:estimator-handle be instantiated so that all retained outcome-wavelet coefficients admit one joint nonasymptotic negative-Besov risk bound, uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M(d,m,\alpha,\beta,s,L)\), even when the scale-dependent covariate projection rank exceeds \(n\), with every higher-order degenerate variance and pilot remainder controlled without imposing mixed \((x,y)\)-derivatives?
body.justification: This is the first changed proof step from scalar higher-order influence functions and the central feasibility bottleneck for an attaining probability-valued estimator.
body.gap: RobinsEtAl2017HOIF controls scalar missing-response functionals, and KennedyBalakrishnanWasserman2023 fixes projection dimension; neither sums high-rank corrections over a growing multiresolution law-valued dictionary.
body.consumer: A positive certificate yields a finite known-design reconstruction benchmark that can be implemented beside DoubleGen, DecFM, and npcausal.

obligation.what_is_open: A joint nonasymptotic negative-Besov risk bound for all retained outcome coefficients when the scale-dependent covariate rank exceeds the sample size.
obligation.obstruction: The full-rank finite-order degenerate correction has covariance contractions with positive powers of rank divided by sample size. The frozen class supplies neither mixed covariate-outcome smoothness nor spectral decay, and deterministic inverse-remainder control does not bound these stochastic contractions. Assuming the desired certificate would assume the crux of the OEQ.
obligation.attempted: Expanded the sign-mixture lower experiment exactly, isolated the two higher-order likelihood terms, and closed probability reconstruction from any signed coefficient bound. For the upper construction, examined the direct finite-order Neumann correction; its high-rank degenerate terms do not yield a uniform summable bound by the available sectional Hölder estimates.
obligation.partial_result: The probability reconstruction part is closed: once a signed unit-mass coefficient estimate \(\widetilde Q\) obeys a joint Kantorovich--Rubinstein error bound, \(\texttt{lem:kr-probability-projection}\) returns an actual probability measure with no more than twice that error plus the chosen grid mesh.  The unresolved step is earlier.  For a covariate projection of rank \(K_j>n\), a direct order-\(p\) Neumann (U)-statistic expansion contains degenerate contractions whose second moments include positive powers of \(K_j/n\).  The deterministic Galerkin remainder does not control those terms, and none of the frozen assumptions supplies a low-rank, mixed-smoothness, or spectral-decay condition that would remove them.  Thus no uniform joint negative-Besov certificate has been proved for the construction in \(\texttt{def:estimator-handle}\).
